newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin in the dark on Yeltsin's cabinet plans.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin in the dark on Yeltsin's cabinet plans.

text.p: The Kremlin spokesman said on Wednesday that he had no information on the changes President Boris Yeltsin plans to make when he reshuffles his government team and could not confirm rumours that top officials could go.

"I have no information confirming that any dismissal is planned of anyone occupying an important post in the government," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference. Some Russian newspapers had said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin could be ousted.
Yastrzhembsky said earlier this week that the reshuffle would not include Chernomyrdin, who is viewed in financial markets as the best guarantor of Russia's economic reform course.
"I think best of all would be to be patient and wait," Yastrzhembsky said.
Yeltsin told Chernomyrdin on Monday that a cabinet reshuffle might help improve the situation in the country, and the news triggered a wave of rumours over which ministers might be sacked.
The liberal Izvestia newspaper said it would be Chernomyrdin himself. Itar-Tass news agency on Wednesday singled out Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and said he might be ousted in March.
